body:
## 🎯 Triage report

Feature request to expand the default Guest OS list with newer major versions of common Linux distributions (AlmaLinux/Rocky 10, Debian 13, Ubuntu newer LTS, etc.) so admins don't need to add them manually after each release.

### 📊 Assessment

| Dimension | Value | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| **Type** | `type:new-feature` | Requests new default data (guest OS mappings), not a bug fix |
| **Component** | none | Affects the guest OS type list, which spans management-server config data rather than a single clearly identifiable component |
| **Severity** | n/a | Not a bug |
| **Labels** | `type:new-feature` | See above |
| **Coding agent** | Needs more info | The general idea is clear, but a concrete PR would require enumerating exact distro/version/hypervisor guest-OS-mapping entries to add (per hypervisor: KVM, VMware, XenServer), which isn't specified here |

### 🔗 Similar issues

- https://github.com/apache/cloudstack/issues/12374 (related) — explicit request to add Debian 13 (trixie) support to the guest OS list, a subset of this broader request

<details><summary>💡 Notes and suggestions</summary>

- The default guest OS list is defined in DB seed data (e.g. `engine/schema/src/main/resources/META-INF/db/schema-*` and `guest_os`/`guest_os_hypervisor` tables) — historically new OS types are added via SQL upgrade scripts per major release.
- Consider asking the reporter to specify exactly which OS/version combinations they need (e.g. AlmaLinux 10, Rocky Linux 10, Ubuntu 24.04 already exists per issue text, Ubuntu 25.x, Debian 13) and for which hypervisors, to scope a concrete PR.
- Related discussion in #12374 shows there is an established process/precedent for adding a single new guest OS via a dedicated PR — this issue could be split into per-OS sub-tasks following that pattern.

</details>
